title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening for private deployments
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private require strong guarantees that keys and encrypted artifacts remain in-region and that admin/authorization actions are auditable. This change completes the RBAC v2 KMS region pinning and audit hardening workstream for Private deployments: 1) enforce KMS key region residency at policy-evaluation time, 2) add end-to-end audit events for KMS key lookup/fallbacks, 3) require explicit policy allow for cross-region KMS operations, and 4) add migration checks and an opt-in enforcement flag with a rollout plan.

What changed: single PR that touches policy evaluation, audit plumbing, installer checks, and e2e tests. Key pieces: - policy-engine: new resolver to evaluate kms:region and kms:residency attributes at request time, returning a clear allow|deny+reason tuple; rejects requests when policy denies cross-region access. - audit: add structured audit events for kms.resolve, kms.fallback, kms.failure, including metadata (requester, resource, resolved_region, resolver_reason, policy_id). Events are emitted to the same audit pipeline used by existing request logs and include trace/span ids for correlation. - installer/upgrade: private-installer now validates customer-configured KMS ARNs/regions during preflight; a compatibility check warns if existing keys are cross-region and suggests migration steps. - config/flags: added rbac.v2.kms_enforce_region (boolean) and rbac.v2.kms_audit_level (info|verbose|off) with sensible defaults (enforce=false during rollout, audit=info). - e2e and unit tests: new test vectors for region mismatches, audit payload assertions, and a smoke test for private installer.

Testing and CI: All unit tests pass locally and on CI. Added ~18 new unit tests and 3 integration test scenarios that run against a locally mocked KMS. CI summary: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e (pass). Nightly regression bench run showed negligible latency impact (<1% p50 for policy eval path under 1000rps).

Security review: expanded threat model covering attacker attempting to use cross-region KMS keys to exfiltrate data; mitigation includes explicit deny semantics, audit alerts, and optional enforcement gate. Security review performed by Maya Li and Samir Patel; follow-up issues created for extended telemetry retention (SEC-412).

Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag (rbac.v2.kms_enforce_region=false), 2) enable audit=verbose for 24 hours to gather metrics and validate events and false-positive rate, 3) enable enforcement in canary private deployments (customer opt-in), 4) enable enforcement by default after 2-week observation window. We will surface migration guidance in the console and run an automated migration assistant for customers that want to rotate keys into the same region.

Release notes: Enforces KMS region pinning and improves audit logging for KMS operations in Private deployments (rbac v2). This adds a new admin configuration flag and conservative rollout; no immediate enforcement unless enabled by operators.

notes_for_ops: Operator: to enable enforcement, set rbac.v2.kms_enforce_region=true in the control-plane config and optionally set rbac.v2.kms_audit_level=verbose for initial validation. Preflight will warn if existing key ARNs are cross-region. See redwood/docs/admin/kms_region_residency.md for migration steps.
